title: Samsung One UI 9.5 Leak Reveals AI-Powered Custom Widgets and Glass-Inspired Design
excerpt: Leaked internal firmware shows Samsung testing 'My Custom Widget' creation, a glassy visual overhaul, and relocated search controls ahead of a likely Galaxy S27 debut.
body:
• Leaked One UI 9.5 firmware reveals a 'My Custom Widget' feature that lets users describe and create personalized home screen widgets using AI
  • Samsung is testing a glass-inspired visual overhaul with shinier borders, drop shadows, and backdrop blurring across UI elements
  • The Phone app gets a relocated search icon in a floating bottom bar, and a native App Lock feature is also in testing
  • One UI 9.5 is expected to debut with the Galaxy S27 series in early 2027

Samsung's next major software update is taking shape months before its expected launch. A leaked internal firmware build of One UI 9.5, obtained and explored by tipster Fahad Ali Javed, reveals two significant additions: an AI-powered custom widget creator and a glass-inspired design language that marks a visual departure from the current interface.

My Custom Widget: AI Meets the Home Screen

The most notable discovery in the leaked build is "My Custom Widget," a feature that appears in the widget picker alongside Samsung's standard options. The leaked screenshot shows a modular, split-layout widget combining calendar and messaging elements in a single tile — with no fixed app anchor required.

The feature mirrors Google's "Create My Widget," announced in May as part of Android's Gemini Intelligence capabilities. Google demonstrated a system where users describe what they want a widget to do in plain language, and the AI assembles it from available app data and shortcuts.

"Samsung is testing a native 'Make your own Widget' / 'My Custom Widget' modular split layout right out of the box. Interactive action deep-links directly in the card."

— Fahad Ali Javed, leaker

Whether Samsung's version is a rebrand of Google's implementation or a competing in-house build remains unclear. The Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Z Flip 8 — Samsung's latest foldables — are the first Galaxy devices to ship with Gemini Intelligence, making them likely candidates for the feature once it rolls out.

Google said in May that Create My Widget would arrive on both Pixel and Galaxy devices by the end of summer 2026. If My Custom Widget is indeed Samsung's version of the same feature, it may initially support only native Samsung apps before expanding to third-party integrations.

Glass-Inspired Design Overhaul

The same leaked firmware reveals a subtle but deliberate visual refresh across One UI 9.5. Floating tab bars, the Now Brief widget, header action buttons, and volume sliders all feature shinier borders and drop shadow effects that give the interface a glass-like depth.

Some interface elements blur when placed over other objects, creating visual separation between foreground controls and the background. The effect is reminiscent of Apple's "Liquid Glass" design language introduced in iOS, though Samsung's approach appears more restrained.

Samsung had paused visual updates with One UI 9.0, focusing instead on feature additions. The 9.5 build signals a return to design iteration — an acknowledgment that the Android interface race is increasingly fought on aesthetics as much as functionality.

Phone App Redesign and App Lock

Among the functional changes, Samsung has moved the search icon in the Phone app from the top-right corner to a floating navigation bar at the bottom of the screen. The dialer also gains integrated Samsung AI search capabilities, functioning similarly to the system-wide Finder tool for pulling up contacts, past interactions, and contextual actions directly from the keypad.

A separate leak from the same firmware confirmed that Samsung is adding a native App Lock feature, letting users protect individual applications using a password or biometric authentication directly from the home screen or app drawer — without third-party security apps.

Timeline and Caveats

These features come from early internal testing firmware and could change substantially before release. Samsung typically follows a predictable cadence: One UI 9.5 is expected to debut alongside the Galaxy S27 series in early 2027, with a broader rollout to eligible existing devices in the first half of the year.

Samsung has yet to roll out the stable One UI 9.0 update for existing devices, so the 9.5 leaks are running well ahead of the company's public release schedule. For Galaxy owners, the takeaway is that Samsung's AI and design ambitions for next year are already being baked into early builds — with custom widgets and a visual refresh as the headline additions.
